name: Martin of Tours
legacy: His monastery at Marmoûtiers became the training ground for many Celtic missions and missionaries.

checks.lead: Martin of Tours (Latin: Martinus Turonensis; 316/336 – 8 November 397) was the third bishop of Tours. He is the patron saint of many communities and organizations across Europe, including of the former French Third Republic. A native of Savaria, Pannonia, he converted to Christianity at a young age. He served in the Roman cavalry in Gaul, but left military service prior to 361, when he became a disciple of Hilary of Poitiers, establishing the monastery at Ligugé. He was consecrated as Bishop of Caesarodunum (Tours) in 371. As bishop, he was active in the expansion of the Nicene Creed, yet he was against the violent persecution that fellow nicenes launched against the Priscillianists.
